summary: Collapse the Namias portfolio into a true single-page application. The root page is a self-contained resume-style site where every section (hero, about, experience, projects, contact, blog) is inline or triggered as a modal. Remove the /blog and /blog/[slug] routes entirely; old URLs 301-redirect to / with an auto-open modal query parameter. Keep /studio (Sanity CMS) and /api/* (backend). The result: simplicity, direct access, and a resume-like reading flow.
narrative: The portfolio is a Next.js 16 App Router site with Sanity CMS. The current public surface is /, /blog, /blog/[slug], and /studio. The / route already has all the resume-like sections inline (hero, about, tech stack, projects, experience, connect, certifications, gallery). The /blog and /blog/[slug] pages are full-page routes that compete for attention and add SEO/spam surface. The owner wants a clean resume-style experience: scroll once, see everything, and have blog content available as a modal without leaving the page. This refactor removes the /blog routes, wires blog content into two stacked modals (list + detail), updates all internal links to open modals instead of navigating, and adds 301 redirects for SEO preservation. The visual layout (two-column 62%/38% grid) stays intact — only the routing and modal wiring change.
principles: One scroll, one page — visitors should never need to leave / to consume any content.
Modals, not routes — long-form content (blog, contact, booking) is presented in modals, not new pages.
Preserve SEO — old /blog and /blog/[slug] URLs 301 to / with a query param that auto-opens the right modal.
Resume-like readability — keep the existing 62%/38% two-column grid; sections flow top to bottom.
No new public surface — the only public routes are /, /studio, and /api/*. No new pages.
Each slice is a commit — page removal, modal creation, link rewiring, redirects, sitemap, tests, docs are all separate commits.
No behaviour change for studio/api — Sanity CMS and backend routes are untouched.

epics.title: Build blog modals

stories.details: Create src/components/ui/BlogListModal.tsx. Use the existing Modal primitive. Read blogPosts from useCmsContent. Render a scrollable list of cards. Each card opens BlogPostModal with the post slug.

stories.title: Create BlogPostModal component
stories.details: Create src/components/ui/BlogPostModal.tsx. Use the existing Modal primitive. Take a slug prop. Find the post in useCmsContent.blogPosts. Render title, date, readTime, tags, coverImage, body (portableTextToMarkdown or similar). Back button returns to the list.

stories.title: Mount the new modals in ModalProvider
stories.details: Update src/hooks/useModal.tsx to mount BlogListModal and BlogPostModal. Extend the ModalName union type to include 'blog' and 'blog-post'. Track activeBlogSlug in context state.

epics.title: Rewire internal links
epics.summary: Replace every href='/blog' and Link to /blog with a button or trigger that opens the blog modal. Remove the now-unused BlogListClient and BlogPostContent components (or keep them as modal internals).

stories.title: Rewire HubMenu blog link to open the modal
stories.details: Update src/components/ui/HubMenu.tsx: change the 'Read Blog' item to call openModal('blog') on click instead of navigating to /blog.

stories.title: Rewire HeroSection blog CTA to open the modal
stories.details: Update src/components/sections/HeroSection.tsx: change the 'Read blog' link to call openModal('blog') on click.

stories.title: Remove or repurpose BlogListClient and BlogPostContent

epics.title: Delete /blog routes and add 301 redirects
epics.summary: Delete src/app/blog/page.tsx and src/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx. Add a 301 redirect from /blog and /blog/[slug] to /?modal=blog[&slug=...]. Use next.config.js redirects.

stories.title: Delete the /blog routes
stories.details: Remove src/app/blog/page.tsx and src/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx (and the blog directory if empty).

stories.title: Auto-open the blog modal on root when ?modal= is set
stories.details: In the root page or a small client wrapper, read the URL search params on mount. If modal=blog, call openModal('blog'). If modal=blog and slug is set, call openModal('blog-post', slug) and also open the list behind it (or just open the post directly).
